- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.8) but price declines sharply, model overreacts; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if sentiment drops below 0.6.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.5–0.8) and price trend is downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent 10-day low.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–4% if sentiment >0.8 but price drops >2% from prior day.
